query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy provides a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor integrity and tends to crack. Prior studies on related MM′X materials used epoxy-containing Mn0.98CoGe, obtaining compressive strengths of 152 and 218 MPa at two epoxy contents, and low-melting In composites, obtaining 48 MPa compressive strength and more than eight times the thermal conductivity of epoxy-containing samples under the reported conditions. These routes demonstrated gains in selected strength or heat-transport metrics, but the desired coexistence of robust integrity and high caloric performance remains unresolved. The target should also remain rare-earth-free. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing caloric response? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, quantitative or directional outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, boundary conditions under applied-field, pressure, temperature, and loading regimes, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive controlled experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A controlled post‐high-pressure torsion (HPT) annealing treatment will induce a refined dual‐phase microstructure in (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38, thereby reinforcing its mechanical integrity (i.e. reducing cracking and increasing compressive strength) without sacrificing its large caloric response.
generation.material_initial_state: As-sintered (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy that displays high caloric performance but suffers from poor integrity and cracking.
generation.intervention: Apply a controlled annealing treatment following high-pressure torsion processing.
generation.conditions: Under operating conditions that involve applied magnetic or pressure fields and the temperature regime where the caloric transformation is active; annealing parameters (temperature and time) must be optimized to maintain the phase responsible for the caloric effect while promoting microstructural refinement.
generation.structural_mediator: A dual-phase microstructure consisting of a fine, recrystallized phase interspersed with retained metastable regions that resist crack propagation.
generation.mechanism: The annealing reduces residual stress and refines the grain structure, leading to a heterogeneous microstructure that acts to arrest crack propagation and improve mechanical robustness, while the transformation mechanism underlying caloric performance remains largely intact.
generation.predicted_outcome: The intervention is predicted to significantly improve mechanical properties (e.g., an estimated 50–100% increase in compressive strength and enhanced fracture toughness) while retaining at least ~90% of the original caloric response magnitude compared to the unchanged alloy.
generation.baseline: The unmodified (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy, which exhibits excellent caloric effects but poor structural integrity manifesting as cracking under stress.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis applies under the same applied-field, pressure, temperature, and loading regimes typical for operating caloric devices, with annealing parameters carefully chosen to avoid altering the phase transformation kinetics responsible for the caloric effect.
generation.uncertainty: The precise optimization window (annealing temperature and duration) required to achieve the ideal balance between mechanical toughness and caloric performance is uncertain until systematically calibrated.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sample sets of (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38: one set undergoes high-pressure torsion followed by the controlled annealing treatment intended to produce the refined dual-phase microstructure, and the other set remains unannealed as a control. Subject both sets to identical applied-field and pressure-field cycling while monitoring their caloric performance and mechanical integrity.
measurements: Compression testing to quantify yield strength and fracture toughness
Caloric performance measurements (e.g., adiabatic temperature change or entropy change) using calorimetry/DSC
Microstructural characterization (grain size distribution, phase identification via XRD)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the annealed samples fail to show a statistically significant improvement in mechanical strength and crack resistance (e.g., less than a 50% increase over the control) or if they exhibit a reduction of more than 10% in caloric output relative to the control, the hypothesis will be falsified.

cited_evidence.text: AbstractAnnealing of severely plastic deformed materials is expected to produce a good combination of strength and ductility, which has been widely demonstrated in conventional materials. In the present study, high-pressure torsion processed CoCrNi medium entropy alloy consisting of a single face-centered cubic (FCC) phase with a grain size of ~50 nm was subjected to different annealing conditions, and its effect on microstructure and mechanical behavior was investigated. The annealing of high-pressure torsion processed CoCrNi alloy exhibits partial recrystallization and near full recrystallization based on the annealing temperature and time. The samples annealed at 700 °C for 2 min exhibit very fine grain size, a high fraction of low angle grain boundaries, and high kernel average misorientation value, indicating partially recrystallized microstructure. The samples annealed for a longer duration (>2 min) exhibit relatively larger grain size, a low fraction of low angle grain boundaries, and low kernel average misorientation value, indicating nearly full recrystallized microstructure. reading.lever: Apply controlled annealing post-HPT to induce a refined dual-phase microstructure that toughens the alloy without altering its caloric transformation.
reading.why: This intervention, proven in a related medium-entropy system for boosting integrity, shows promise for preserving high caloric response in the MM′X alloy.
